"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/add-strings/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

415. Add Strings

Given two non-negative integers, num1 and num2 represented as string, return the sum of num1 and num2 as a string.

You must solve the problem without using any built-in library for handling large integers (such as BigInteger). You must also not convert the inputs to integers directly.

Example 1:

Input: num1 = "11", num2 = "123"
Output: "134"

Example 2:

Input: num1 = "456", num2 = "77"
Output: "533"

Example 3:

Input: num1 = "0", num2 = "0"
Output: "0"

Constraints:

    1 <= num1.length, num2.length <= 10^4
    num1 and num2 consist of only digits.
    num1 and num2 don't have any leading zeros except for the zero itself.
"""


class Solution:
    def addStrings(self, num1: str, num2: str) -> str:
        i, j = len(num1) - 1, len(num2) - 1
        carry = 0
        res = []
        while i >= 0 or j >= 0 or carry:
            x1 = ord(num1[i]) - ord("0") if i >= 0 else 0
            x2 = ord(num2[j]) - ord("0") if j >= 0 else 0
            value = x1 + x2 + carry
            carry = value // 10
            res.append(str(value % 10))
            i -= 1
            j -= 1
        return "".join(res[::-1])


sol = Solution()

print(sol.addStrings("11", "123"))  # "134"

assert sol.addStrings("11", "123") == "134"
assert sol.addStrings("456", "77") == "533"
assert sol.addStrings("0", "0") == "0"

assert sol.addStrings("1", "9") == "10"
assert sol.addStrings("999", "1") == "1000"
assert sol.addStrings("123456789", "987654321") == "1111111110"
assert sol.addStrings("0", "99999999999999999999") == "99999999999999999999"
assert sol.addStrings("5000", "5000") == "10000"
assert (
    sol.addStrings("10000000000000000000", "10000000000000000000")
    == "20000000000000000000"
)
assert (
    sol.addStrings("12345678901234567890", "98765432109876543210")
    == "111111111011111111100"
)
assert sol.addStrings("0", "1") == "1"
assert sol.addStrings("99999999999999999999", "0") == "99999999999999999999"
assert sol.addStrings("500", "500") == "1000"
assert sol.addStrings("123", "456") == "579"
